Distributed infrastructure will be very difficult to affect with ddos.

This is no surprise. DDoSing is the most basic way to bring any server down.

Imagine people in line getting ready to enter a restaurant. These "people" represent packets. Normally, everything runs smoothly. Traffic fluctuates, but nothing is too much. A DDoS attack is simply when too many people get in line and begin to force their way in to the restaurant. Obviously, the establishment would break down do to being overfilled and then have to pitch itself up again once things got going. The restaurant is like a server.

That's all it is. To DDoS google.com, all you need are enough computers connecting to google (which means sending packets) to get to the point where google's servers are no longer capable of handling the load. Now adays access to computers is growing which gives DDoS attacks strength. DDoS has strength in numbers, but is not complicated nor does it require much knowledge about computers. It is essentially baby's first hack.

Just type "ping google.com -t" (without quotes) in a command prompt in windows and watch. That is all it is just with many, many more computers. Close the command prompt to stop sending packets.
